# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 38 (Bi-Vb Pc38)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc38
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 38
**Title (English, from literature):** Wandering outside the country
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tiroraṭṭha-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 38) governs the conduct of Buddhist nuns regarding travel abroad. According to the rule, an expiation offense (*pācittiya*) is incurred by any nun who travels without an accompanying group of travelers in an insecure or dangerous region outside the country or kingdom (*tiroraṭṭhe*) [Hüsken 1997]. As Ute Hüsken notes, the rule closely parallels Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 37, differing crucially only in the geographical scope specified: while Pācittiya 37 governs dangerous travel within the realm in which the nun resides, Pācittiya 38 specifies traveling beyond that territory (*tiroraṭṭhe*) [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken characterizes these adjacent precepts as rules functioning for the protection of nuns against physical assault and rape (*dūsesum*) by robbers along lonely roads [Hüsken 1997]. The word-for-word commentary (*padabhājanīya*) for this rule—shared with Pācittiyas 38 and 39—stipulates that the offense is accrued upon entering each neighboring village, or for every half-*yojana* walked through an uninhabited forest area [Hüsken 1997].

 Machine-assisted textual reuse analysis confirms near-verbatim structural identity between Pācittiya 38 and Pācittiya 37 (sharing 3,117 characters across §§0.1–2.22), as well as extensive formulaic reuse across other travel and procedural rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (especially Pācittiyas 39, 24, 84, and 41) [DharmaNexus]. Textual reuse algorithms also align the text with Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda commentarial literature, including the *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112) and the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus].
